primary_classification.classification_basis: Inferential Evidence–Authority Conflation is supported in this occurrence because In this occurrence, an uncertain facial-recognition match was reportedly allowed to contribute to coercive public action without adequate independent identity corroboration and timely contestability.

assessment_boundaries: Legal Aid's statements about wrongfulness, bias and policy violations are preserved as attributable claims, not adopted as judicial findings.
VIGIL has not independently reviewed the underlying DD5 and ECMS records on which Legal Aid relies.
The precise SAU facial-recognition tool and database remain unresolved in the public evidence.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Legal Aid Society reports from its review of NYPD records that the Facial Identification Section first returned no match for the surveillance material; hours later a possible match was entered that Legal Aid says came from the Special Activities Unit rather than FIS. The letter states that the possible match led to Trevis Williams's arrest even though he did not match the victim's physical description, and it records unresolved questions about what database, tool and approval the Special Activities Unit used. These propositions are attributed to Legal Aid and are not represented as a judicial finding.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence raises both inferential-authority and provenance concerns. A later facial-recognition result should not silently displace an earlier no-match without exposing the changed method, database, operator and authorisation basis. And a 'possible match' should remain defeasible when independent physical-description evidence cuts against it. Human processing cannot supply reliable assurance if decision-makers cannot see how the second inference was generated or what materially changed between the two searches.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000007 demonstrates that contestability depends on provenance as well as human review. A consequential identity inference should carry enough lineage to show who generated it, using what authorised source set and method, and why it differs from prior results; otherwise downstream investigators cannot calibrate its evidentiary authority.
